items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: did you know Dean Alfange, a member of my class? I hadn’t seen Dean since I graduated... we sat and talked and drank a glass of wine

ctx.x: No but I enjoy hearing about — of course I should tell — my daughter went to Hamilton, she just graduated last May so I really enjoy hearing about what it was like back then.

Yeah, well Hamilton was a conservative college, and it still is. And did you know Dean Alfange, a member of my class? I hadn’t seen Dean since I graduated. I went back for my fiftieth, and Dean came over and said “Jim, I don’t know whether you remember me.” And I said “sure Dean, nice to see you.” And we sat and talked and drank a glass of wine and he had said something nice about one of my books. And I asked, because his father had been head of the — I’m not sure, one of the labor parties, whether it was the…
went here.” So that was somebody I think had sponsored him, an immigrant or something like this sponsored him and he came. I mean you’d have to ask Dean the details.
